svg.text: SONIC-Academy · illustrated action guide
Roll back safely when a check fails
Teaching diagram · not a screenshot or actual terminal result
APP01 · IIS Manager, recovery record and isolated lab
Stop PracticeHelpdesk first and record the failed check and new errors. Keep the candidate
folder/logs for investigation. Do not restore a whole-VM checkpoint or overwrite the database
as the first response to a PHP mapping problem.
Check the previous runtime against the security advisory BEFORE putting it back into service.
If it is older than the fixed minimum or otherwise vulnerable, leave the live pool stopped.
Investigate that old runtime only on an isolated copy with no user traffic, or repair the
patched candidate. Availability is not permission to reopen vulnerable PHP.
If the previous runtime is still security-approved, select this site → Handler Mappings → PHP-
FastCGI → Edit and restore its recorded previous executable. Restore only its recorded
candidate-specific FastCGI/environment settings and the previous protected php.ini if those
were changed. Do not remove an entry used by another website.
Restart only this pool and repeat the web-served version and every acceptance check. Reopen
only when the old runtime remains patched and the application passes. Otherwise stop it again
and keep a maintenance notice or unavailable service.
A PHP-only mapping rollback normally does not need a database restore. If
application/schema/data changes also occurred, stop and use a separately approved application-
consistent restore plan; restoring an older database can erase new tickets. Restore server-wide
IIS configuration only after checking the effect on every site.
Record the rollback decision, exact runtime/configuration restored, ticket/data checks and next
corrective action. Never mark a failed patch successful merely because you rolled back.
Check: The app is either healthy on a security-approved runtime or remains unavailable pending
a safe fix. No vulnerable runtime was returned to service.
